newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends mixed ahead of elections.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends mixed ahead of elections.

text.p: Mexican peso contracts closed mixed on Thursday after players squared their books ahead of a long weekend for U.S. markets and mid-term elections on July 6, traders said.
"It looked very much as though dealers squared positions to close their books before the elections," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso closed 0.4 of a centavo firmer at 7.9570/7.9610 per dollar while its 24-hour stablemate ended 0.4 of a centavo softer at 7.9550/7.9590 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts had closed earlier 0.8 of a centavo firmer at 7.9300/7.9330 per dollar.

Mexicans vote on Sunday for an new lower house of Congress, a quarter of the Senate, six state governors and, for the first time, a mayor of Mexico City. Previously, that post has been filled by a presidential nominee.
Dealers said dollars were in greater demand at 24 hours because they would not require settlement until Monday, as U.S. financial markets will close on Friday for the Independence Day holiday.
The peso had gained ground in early trade on favorable reaction in the U.S. bond market to U.S. employment data.
"U.S. data moved bolstered the U.S. long bond and that propped up the peso," a dealer said. "But then local and foreign investors stepped in to buy dollars to square their books.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was up 35/32 to yield 6.62 percent as Mexican foreign exchange markets were closing.
Dealers said the peso could weaken on Friday due to lack of dollars in the market.
"There will be no trade on U.S.. markets tomorrow, but many can work at peso desks, although only for a short while," a trader said. "The peso could come under pressure."
